brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A tea from Yushan county in Jiangxi with geographical indication status, named for Mount Sanqing. It is called white for its mostly bud-only leaf thickly covered in silvery down.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: Its production is said to go back to the Tang, to have flourished in the Song, and to have led Jiangxi in output by the late Qing. It won the top prize at the 2011 Zhongcha Cup national tea competition and provincial gold awards in 2011 and 2012.
processing: Typical of green tea: picked, heated soon after picking to stop oxidation, then shaped and dried.
harvest_season: Usually picked in spring, with the earliest pickings prized, as with most green teas.
appearance_dry: Straight, tightly formed strands, bud-heavy and downy, in a fresh yellow-green.
appearance_wet: Jade-white leaf flesh with emerald veins.
taste_profile: Rich aroma, a fresh and lively taste, and a lingering sweetness that draws saliva.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
